source_text: Consequens enim esse - existimas - ut sensum videndi, audiendi, gustandi, olfaciendi, atque tangendi, non a Deo, sed a diabolo nobis fateamur esse collatum; si concesserimus eam concupiscentiam carnis, cui per continentiam repugnamus, non fuisse in paradiso ante peccatum, et ex illo accidisse peccato, quod primum primo homini diabolus persuasiti
pass_a_gloss: Consequens for to-be - existimas - so-that/as sensum videndi, audiendi, gustandi, olfaciendi, and tangendi, not from to-God, but from to-the-devil to-us fateamur to-be collatum; if concesserimus her desire of-flesh, to-whom through continentiam repugnamus, not to-have-been in paradiso before sin, and from illo accidisse by-sin, that/which first first to-the-human the-devil persuasiti.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: It follows that we must confess that our senses of sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch were given to us by the devil rather than by God, if we concede that the desire of the flesh against which we struggle through self-restraint was not in paradise before sin, but arose from the first sin which the devil persuaded the first human being to commit.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
